key_insight: A two-flexible-plate channel with Poiseuille flow exhibits a critical-layer structural-acoustic instability: the symmetric wall mode becomes convectively unstable above a Mach-number threshold, while the antisymmetric mode is symmetry-protected and remains unabsorbed.
engineering_relevance: This result helps predict when compliant ducts or channels may amplify pressure fluctuations and fail due to flow-induced wall-mode instability, especially in low-Mach compressible designs.
method: Closed-form O(M) correction for coupled wavenumbers using Fredholm solvability
Critical-layer analysis of symmetric vs. antisymmetric wall modes
Briggs-Bers classification to distinguish convective instability from other mechanisms
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement among three independent numerical schemes to one part in 10^9 and matching between the closed-form correction and numerical differentiation across three shear profiles.
watch_item: The instability depends on compliant-wall dynamics and the appearance of an interior critical layer, so rigid-wall assumptions or regimes below the critical Mach number will miss the effect entirely.
paper_title: A critical-layer instability of structural acoustic wall modes in a two-flexible-plate channel with Poiseuille flow: closed-form low-Mach corrections and parity-protected absorption
